essence: Octavia, the spider-web city, is a net slung between two mountain crests over a deep chasm; the net is both street and foundation, everything else hangs beneath it, and its people live with less doubt than others because they know the net will not hold forever.
textDetails: Octavia is called the spider-web city.
It lies over a precipice between two steep mountains, out over the void, bound to both crests by ropes, chains and catwalks.
People walk on small wooden ties, taking care not to step into the gaps, or they hold on to the hemp strands.
Below there is nothing for hundreds and hundreds of feet (in Weaver's English); a few clouds glide past, and farther down the bed of the chasm can be glimpsed.
The city's base is a net that serves both as passageway and as support.
Everything else, instead of rising above the base, hangs below it.
Hanging below: rope ladders, hammocks, houses shaped like sacks, clothes hangers, terraces like gondolas, skins full of water.
Also hanging: gas jets, roasting spits, baskets on strings, dumbwaiters, showers.
Also hanging: trapezes and rings for children's games, cable cars, chandeliers, and pots of plants with trailing foliage.
Suspended over the abyss, the inhabitants' life is less uncertain than in other cities.
They are aware that the net can only hold for so long.
Not in the text: the rock of the mountains, the net's exact pattern, the light, the season or the number of inhabitants; the radial orb-web pattern is a design reading of 'spider-web'.
visualConcept: Two sheer mountain crests of dark slate-blue rock rise out of a sea of cloud on either side of a deep chasm, their tops still burning with the last light, their faces dropping away into blue shadow. Strung between them, just below the crest line, is the net: a vast, slightly sagging horizontal spider web of hemp, with radial main ropes running from a central hub to about two dozen anchor points on the two cliff faces (fixed with iron rings, chains and short timber catwalks), crossed by a spiral of thinner strands, and with narrow walkways of little wooden ties laid along the main radials and around the hub. Nothing stands on the net except tiny walkers picking their way across the ties; everything that makes a city hangs beneath it on ropes of different lengths: plump houses shaped like sacks with round lit windows, terraces like gondolas holding people and potted plants, hammocks, rope ladders, laundry on clothes hangers, bulging water skins, small gas flames, spits, baskets on strings, dumbwaiter boxes, showers, children's trapezes and rings, crystal chandeliers glittering in open air, and pots trailing long green tendrils. Cable cars hang from cables strung crest to crest beneath the net and glide across the void. Seen from the side the hanging city is an inverted skyline, a chandelier of a town, densest under the hub and thinning toward the cliffs; seen from above it is a web beaded with dew. Far below, clouds drift past under the lowest sack-houses, and through their gaps, very far down, a thin glinting stream marks the chasm's bed, making the depth unmistakable.
layout: Coordinates: the net is the ground plane at y=0. Chasm: runs along z, with cliff faces at about x=-17 and x=+17 (irregular, with ledges), crests rising to y=+7 to +12 and the faces dropping to y=-80, fading into fog below y=-30; the mountains continue beyond the 24-unit city radius as background masses. Net: an orb web with its hub at the origin, about 34 units across (x) by 28 (z), sagging to y=-1.2 at the hub along a catenary; 24 radial main ropes (12 per side) to anchors on the cliff faces at y=+0.5 to +3; spiral strand pitch 0.35; wooden ties (0.3 x 0.06) along 8 main radials and 3 concentric rings as walkways; anchor hardware of chains plus 6 short timber catwalks bridging from ledges onto the net. Hanging city: about 70 sack-houses (teardrop forms 0.5-1.1 tall) on ropes 0.5-6 long; 10 gondola terraces (boat-shaped decks 1.2-2 long) on four ropes each; 30 hammocks; 25 rope ladders 2-8 long; 20 clothes hangers with cloth; 30 water skins; 40 gas jets (small flames on hanging pipes); 8 spits; 40 baskets on strings; 6 dumbwaiters (boxes 0.3 wide on rope loops 3-6 long); 12 showers; 10 trapezes and 8 pairs of rings with child figures; 12 chandeliers (0.3-0.6, crystal sparkle); 40 pots with trailing plants. Distribution: densest within radius 10 of the hub, hanging down to about y=-11. Cable cars: 3 sagging cables crest to crest at y=-4 to -6, 2 cabins each. Clouds: a broken layer of soft volumetric billboards between y=-14 and y=-24, drifting along z. Chasm bed: a narrow stream ribbon at y=-80 with a faint specular glint. People: about 60 walkers 0.25 tall on the ties and in the terraces, plus children on the rings.
signatureMotion: 1) The web breathes: a slow wind wave (period about 14 s) rolls across the net, lifting and dropping it by up to 0.3 units at the hub, and every hanging object answers as a pendulum whose period grows with its rope length, so the whole inverted city sways in staggered, lagging rhythms, ladders and tendrils trailing behind. 2) The traffic of a suspended life: cable cars glide crest to crest (about 40 s per crossing), dumbwaiters rise and fall, children swing on trapezes and rings, laundry flutters, walkers step carefully from tie to tie, and gas flames and chandeliers flicker brighter as the light fades. 3) Clouds stream beneath the city in slow layers, now and then a wisp rising between the sack-houses, opening brief windows onto the glinting chasm bed far below.
interactionDescription: Swings the camera down through the cloud layer to a point deep in the chasm, looking straight up: the net becomes a dark lace of hemp against the bright sky, and the hanging city reads as what it is, a city whose towers all point downward, its sack-houses, chandeliers and trailing plants silhouetted like fruit and dew on a web, cable cars crossing overhead, gas flames and lit windows glowing. Clouds slide past close to the lens. Toggle again to climb back to the crest view.
mood: The moment just after the sun leaves the chasm: the crest tops still glow rose-gold with alpenglow, the sky is clear cold blue overhead and apricot at the horizon, the net and its hanging city sit in luminous blue shade, and the cloud sea below holds the last pink light. Gas flames and chandeliers are just being lit, small warm points against the blue. Thin, cold, very clear air; vertiginous yet serene, light as a held breath.
caption: Octavia hangs in a chasm like a web across a doorway. You cross it on wooden slats, minding the gaps, with clouds passing beneath your feet, and everything a city needs is slung underneath: houses swollen like sacks, terraces rocking like boats, lamps, laundry, ladders, a child turning on a ring above the void. Life here is steadier than on solid ground, because no one pretends the net is forever.
motto: A limit you can see is a kind of ground.
camera: Crest-level view along the chasm: camera on the chasm axis about 44 units from the hub and about 9 units above the net (elevation about 12 degrees), target (0, -4, 0), so the two cliff walls frame the left and right edges, the net is seen in perspective across the upper third, the hanging city fills the middle and the cloud sea the bottom; FOV about 40, slow sideways drift along z.
